title: Microbiology
description: Morphology and physiology of microorganisms with emphasis on the important roles that microbes play in human life. Mechanisms of pathogenicity, host-parasite relationships, the immune response and principles of disease transmission. Techniques of microbial control including sterilization, aseptic procedures, use of disinfectants, antiseptics and chemotherapy. Basic laboratory skills of microbiology.
outcomes: Compare and contrast pathogenicity and the role of normal flora, opportunistic and obligate pathogens in both health and disease state.
Distinguish between bacterial, viral and eukaryotic microbes in terms of structure and chemotherapeutic interventions.
Map out host responses to pathogenic microbes and vaccines.
objectives: Compare and contrast eukaryotic, bacterial and viral organisms
Describe basic microbial metabolic processes and discuss their significance
Discuss basic genetic principles and their potential applications
Discuss the role of the human microbiome in healthy and disease states
Examine common human and animal diseases
Discuss health disparities and the social determinants of health in the U.S. and worldwide as related to infectious disease
Consider the role of microorganisms in the disease process
Compare and contrast antimicrobial drugs used to treat bacterial, viral, protozoan and helminthic diseases
Identify the role of the host organism in resisting infectious diseases
Discuss the importance of vaccines as a public health tool
Evaluate the reliability of scientific information
Exhibit understanding of the scientific method
Use light microscopy to examine and identify microorganisms
Use basic microbiology laboratory techniques to isolate and cultivate microbes in various media and growing conditions
Explore and use biotechnology techniques common in microbiology laboratories
content: History of microbiology, acknowledging that the recorded history of microbiology is biased toward Eurocentric contributions
Importance of microbes to humans and society, including beyond disease states
Structure and replication of DNA and RNA viruses
Basic applications of microbes in biotechnology
Composition of a healthy microbiome and its role in human health
Disproportionate impact of infectious disease and the impact on the physical, mental, and economic health of communities
Antimicrobial drugs that target each pathogen group
Impact of antibiotic resistance on human health
Common vaccine types and their mechanisms of action
Principles of protection to the individual
Herd immunity as a public health protection
lab: Basic microscopic techniques to visualize microbes and immune cells
Physical methods of control using UV radiation
Chemical control using disinfectants and antiseptics
Antibiotics and antibiotic resistance using disc diffusion
